newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GSM FIRM IN DM 250 MLN INVESTMENT DEALS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GSM FIRM IN DM 250 MLN INVESTMENT DEALS.

text.p: Poland's Era GSM digital cellular phone operator will in mid-1997 sign deals to buy a 250 million marks worth of equipment from two firms -- Sweden's Ericsson and Germany's Siemens AG, Era said in a statement.

"The contract is worth 250 million marks of which each supplier will get about 50 percent. The final division of orders between Siemens and Ericsson will depend on the quality and deadlines for the tasks carried out by the firms," it said.
The statement said the contracts would make Siemens and Ericsson the sole providers of base stations, radiocommunication stations and other equipment for the GSM network until the end of 1998.
"The two companies will install and activate about 1,000 base stations by the end of 1997 and more than 2,000 by the end of 1998," the Era statement said.
It also said Era GSM expected to increase its coverage of Poland to 65 percent of the territory from the current 30 percent.
Era's shareholders include Polish trading and industrial conglomerate Elektrim with a 32.5 percent stake, US West and Deutsche Telecom's subsidiary DeTeMobil holding 22.5 percent stakes each.
